entries.title: The frame
entries.note: The frame as a matte. 2731 x 1536 RGBA. The paper margin and the drawn line are solid, and the window in the middle is transparent, so you drop it straight on top of any frame and it cuts its own window: the artwork shows through and the border and the margin come from this layer. The window edge follows the hand drawn wobble exactly, because it was found by walking outward from the centre of a real drawing until it hit the line, rather than by drawing a rectangle. Cut out of existing artwork, not generated, so it is the same pencil and the same paper as everything it sits on. Move it, scale it, animate it or take it off.

entries.title: The marathon runner, face
entries.note: THIS IS THE MAN. Three studies of his head: front, three quarter, profile. Until today the only description of his face in the whole production was nine generic words, so every frame invented him again and he was a different person in each one. This sheet is the lock. The three things that carry him and must survive into every frame are the flattened bridge of the nose, the wide set deep eyes under a straight brow, and the narrow jaw under wide cheekbones. Individual views are cut out in reference/ for building frames from, because a sheet handed to a frame brings its grid with it.

entries.title: How a layer arrives
entries.note: Anything that moves on its own comes to you as three files, never as one picture. This is the pattern, shown with the frame because the frame is already done. entries.title: Ganesha — the remover of obstacles
entries.note: The film was shot in India and this is its thank you. In Hindu tradition Ganesha removes obstacles, and removing an obstacle is the entire subject of this film: the brake is not a wall, it is a setting, and it can be lifted. He sits on top of Viveka's console, the mixer of all human energies, with a few small oil lamps beside him, Tamil Nadu in feeling. He is never lit specially, never cut to and never mentioned. Anyone who knows will see him. SUPERSEDED 2.9.2026. There is no Ganesha in the story. The passage is a cloud vortex and he appears only on the dedication card at the very end, unannounced, which is what makes it a gift rather than a theme.

entries.title: The stamp — CASE CLOSED
entries.note: A century of settled science, pressed flat onto paper. It is what the film reopens. The stamp is not villainous, it is what happens when an answer is good enough for long enough that nobody asks again. Scene 2.

entries.title: The two cards — 1923 and 1997
entries.note: The old answer and the new one, side by side: an arm, and a brain. Fatigue was in the muscle for seventy four years before anyone looked higher up. The film is the gap between these two cards. Scene 7.

entries.title: The magnifying glass
entries.note: Manan's tool and his posture. He is not a student being taught, he is an investigator looking closer at something everybody already believes they understand. It is also the film's only handheld object that crosses between the photographed world and the drawn one. Scenes 1 and 2.

entries.title: The tanks
entries.note: The body as a factory, and the tanks are full. A man says he is empty while his stores stand untouched behind him. Scarcity that turns out to be policy, not supply. Scene 3.

entries.title: The lever — 95 of 100
entries.note: The centre of the whole film in one object. Effort is not a wall you hit, it is a dial somebody set, and it is sitting at ninety five. A wall cannot be moved. A setting can. Scenes 6 and 8.

entries.title: The single fibre lighting
entries.note: Recruitment, seen from inside. One muscle fibre fires, then the cluster, then the leg, then the whole body. This is the muscle activation motif, and it is the only thing in the film animated at full frame rate. It appears three times, identical each time. Scenes 1, 5 and 6.

entries.title: The key
entries.note: Handed from one palm to another. The brake can be released, but only by someone who has been told it exists. Knowledge as permission, and the reason the film is worth making at all. Scene 8.

entries.title: The finish line behind the trees
entries.note: The goal was always there and could not be seen. The runner is not weak, he is misinformed: he thinks he has ten kilometres left. Motivation is information. Scene 1.

entries.title: Stuck
entries.note: The dying man. Barely moving, visibly stuttering, heavy posterisation. This is the brake fully on, and it is where scene 1 opens. If it looks broken, it is working.

entries.title: The default
entries.note: Everything else in the film. Something is not turning over cleanly. This is the rate the audience learns as normal, which is what makes the other three mean anything.

entries.title: Released
entries.note: He runs. Still stepped, but roughly three times the stuck rate. Nothing is explained and nothing is smooth, yet the eye feels him come loose. Same technique, higher rate, and the change alone carries the release.

entries.title: Alive
entries.note: The muscle activation, and nothing else, ever. Fully smooth. It happens three times in the film and it is the same sequence copy pasted each time: the runner seeing the finish line, Manan on the bicycle, and Viveka naming the limit.

KEY FRAME 1 of 3. He is finished, and he believes he still has ten kilometres to run, which is why the exhaustion is total. Head down, eyes on the ground, mouth open. THE CAMERA DOES NOT MOVE across these three: same head size, same position, same three quarter angle throughout. The emotion changes inside the shot without a cut, so this is the start of one continuous move, not three separate shots. Frame rate here is the slowest in the film, two to three a second, barely turning over. FILED AS 1-4, 3.9.2026, in the reset that gave scene one its final names. entries.note: KEY FRAME 1 of 4 of THE MUSCLE ACTIVATION. Deep inside a muscle, closer than any eye could get. One single fibre ignites and throws a hard star of light across the dark field; every other fibre is still unlit. THE DARKEST FRAME IN THE FILM, mean luminance 152 against about 240 everywhere else, and that darkness is what makes the light mean something. THIS SEQUENCE RUNS AT 25 FRAMES A SECOND, fully smooth, against 2 to 7 everywhere else. entries.title: Style reference — RSA Animate, Cognitive Media
entries.note: THIS IS THE STYLE FOR BOTH THEORY SECTIONS. RSA Animate, drawn by Andrew Park at Cognitive Media. A hand draws the argument on the board while the voice explains it, in real time, and the drawing spreads sideways across the surface instead of being cut to when finished. That live scribing is exactly what we want: Manan's chalk drawing itself as he speaks, then Viveka answering on the whiteboard in black marker. Watch how the hand stays in frame, how pictures and words share one surface, and how the camera drifts across the board rather than cutting. These four were chosen for subject as well as style: the brain, motivation, belief changing outcome, and perception. The most viewed RSA Animates are about economics and education, which look right but say nothing to this film.

Watch how the hand stays in frame, how pictures and words share one surface, and how the camera drifts across the board rather than cutting. These four were chosen for subject as well as style: the brain, motivation, belief changing outcome, and perception. The most viewed RSA Animates are about economics and education, which look right but say nothing to this film.

entries.slug: EXT. THE HOUSE OF THE BODY — DAY
entries.what: The front of a building where nothing is straight. Bone columns bowed narrow at the middle, a roofline of melted stone, windows set deep under heavy brows, one broad low opening with a curved sill, and a single heavy door at ground level.
entries.why: THE BUILDING IS HIS BODY, and it reads as a face without being drawn as one: the windows are eyes, the balcony is a mouth. It replaced a factory, which said industry when the film needed living thing. The style is organic architecture in the manner of Gaudi, and it was got by describing the geometry rather than naming a building, which is the same law that made the organ walls work. entries.what: A vaulted hall with one great smooth vessel standing in it, swelling at the base and narrow at the waist, with rounded tubes leaving it in both directions.
entries.why: REBUILT 31.8.2026 in the language of the house. THE WALLS ARE UNCHANGED and were never the problem: domed muscular chambers with fibrous cords stretched across the hollows. Only the built things changed, and the instruction that did the work was no rivet, bolt, flange or straight edge anywhere. entries.note: THE LUNGS, as ribs and tubing overhead. He looks into every room he passes and in none of them is there anything for him. That is the point of this stretch: the film has to spend real time finding nothing before the key door means anything. Its name before the reset was 8-2-A-v3. ARCHIVED 4.9.2026. entries.slug: INT. THE BODY — THE CONTROL ROOM
entries.what: Viveka seated at a long desk that grows out of the floor on a swelling base, its dials sunk into shallow hollows, the screens in an irregular cluster of rounded openings in the wall, the door arched and soft panelled.
entries.why: REBUILT 31.8.2026 in the language of the house, and it is the deepest room in the body. The clay walls with their shallow winding grooves are unchanged and were always right. THE SCREENS AS CELLS are the detail that matters: the last piece of machinery becomes part of the body. The floor kept rectangular slabs despite being asked three times across three frames; it barely reads and was left.

entries.title: Viveka's desk and chair
entries.note: Four views of the grown desk and its chair: front, three quarter, side, rear. THE SIDE VIEW IS THE USEFUL ONE, it shows the desk and the floor as a single continuous curve, which is what you need to redraw it from any angle. Dials and levers sit down in shallow hollows, never bolted onto a panel, and nothing has a rivet, bolt, flange or straight edge. The chair is a shell on a single stem. ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE ROOM: this sheet draws the screens as part of the console. In the room they are cell-like openings in the clay wall behind it. Keep them in the wall.

entries.what: The doorway very close, filling the frame. Grown stone, arched and wider at the bottom, edges rounded over. Soft irregular slabs run up to a low rounded lip of a sill, and beyond it the paper is blank.
entries.why: REBUILT 31.8.2026 in the language of the house. THE SILL IS STILL ONE DARK LINE and that is the whole point: drawn floor behind it, nothing beyond, which is what lets the next frame be bare paper without reading as a cut to nothing. Measured, the middle of the frame is 100 percent unmarked paper. The flanking doors dropped out and the walls sweep in instead, which is better: fewer objects competing with the opening and the curve pulls the eye through.
entries.title: He is at the door
entries.note: HE IS AT THE DOOR, AND THE DOOR IS GIVING OFF LIGHT. The first frame of the house and the only one with no architecture in it yet: a doorway blown almost to white, the sill and the jamb the only things holding a shape. It is built from an almost empty plate on purpose. The version before it kept the whole doorway and just widened the blank centre, and it read as a drawing of a door rather than as light. He does not walk through this, he is PULLED through it. Its name before the reset was 7-0-A-v2. ARCHIVED 4.9.2026. It was 7-1, drawn before the house had a design: hinged wooden doors, organs chosen because a body has organs, and cables on the ceiling. All three are gone.

The leaves are the same stone as the wall with no rivet, hinge or straight edge, so they read as parts of the building that moved rather than joinery fitted into it. entries.slug: INT. THE BODY — THE SKULL DOOR
entries.what: A closed stone door at the end of a short passage. A softly domed top, one shallow oval push plate on the right at hand height, and an oval plaque at eye height reading VIVEKA.
entries.why: THE SECOND DOOR HE OPENS, and it rhymes with the front door rather than repeating it. A skull is suggested by the dome alone and never drawn: no teeth, no jaw, no sockets. Anyone who has walked the corridor will feel it, nobody is told. THE PLAQUE IS THE ONLY PLACE IN THE FILM THE CHARACTER IS NAMED IN WRITING, and it arrives before he does. The push plate sits where a hand falls and the plaque where an eye falls, because the building is strange but not inconvenient.

entries.title: Title
entries.note: The film opens on its own title, drawn in the film’s hand.

entries.title: The marathon runner
entries.note: A MARATHON RUNNER runs. Not the boy: a man who has done this all his life, which is what makes the question worth asking. The world he runs through is rubbed up out of the paper, nature before anybody stands in it: road, then trees, then shoes, then legs, then the man.

entries.title: He takes the question outside
entries.note: He cannot let it go, so he takes the question outside and puts it on himself. The hero plates for the road and the bicycle: what the world looks like before anybody rides through it. The last daylight in the film.

entries.title: He tests it on the bicycle
entries.note: Curiosity becomes an experiment. He takes the bicycle out on the street and pushes at the limit himself, because a question you can ride is better than a question you can only read.

entries.title: He races himself
entries.note: Indoors, on the trainer, with his own earlier ride playing back on the laptop in front of him. He is racing HIMSELF. There is no opponent, no clock, nobody watching: the only thing he is trying to beat is what his own body did an hour ago, which is exactly the argument the film is about to make. He pushes until he collapses.

entries.title: He closes his eyes
entries.note: He stops, breathes, relaxes. Out to white.

entries.title: The vortex, up
entries.note: He closes his eyes and goes into the light. While he is travelling through it The vortex rises, opens, and is gone, and the white closes around him exactly as it opened. Never explained, never mentioned. Then the light fades down.

entries.title: The house of the body, and the key door
entries.note: The light fades and he is at a door that is already giving off light, and he is pulled through it rather than walking in. Only then does the building assemble around us: halls of organ doors with shapes pressed into the clay and no written names, and nothing behind any of them for him. Then the key, small at the end of a hall, and then the key door filling the frame. ONE UNBROKEN MOVE, seen through his own eyes, with no cut anywhere in it.

entries.title: They introduce each other, and the two theories
entries.note: Inside, one room and one chair and a man who has been expecting him. He asks for something impossible and the whole idea of the film gets done as a party trick. Then the two theories, on the hologram that is already standing in the room: Manan never writes anything, he thinks it and Viveka visualises it, and then Viveka answers in the same places with every value reversed.

entries.title: The conclusion, and goodbye
entries.note: Viveka lets the key go, it falls through an empty frame, and we cut to Manan catching it. THE END.

entries.title: The key
entries.note: THIS IS THE KEY, AND IT IS A REAL OBJECT ON THE LIVE SET. Four views: full side, tilted three quarter, head detail, bit end profile. A long round shaft; at one end a flat round disc with a three lobed clover hole and the number 5 stamped near its edge; a collar of three raised rings where head meets shaft; at the other end a flat rectangular bit with three square teeth. EVERY DRAWN KEY IN THE FILM MUST MATCH THIS. The earlier frames drew a modern flat key and are all wrong: the Viveka character sheet, and the four hand phases 15-1 through 15-4. The point of matching it exactly is that the drawn key and the real key are the same object, so the cross dissolve from drawing to photograph in the last shot lands on itself rather than on something similar. Photographs in reference/key/.

entries.title: Viveka
entries.note: THIS IS VIVEKA. Four views: front, three quarter, side, rear. A brain for a head with no neck, two small eyes and a wide simple smile, zipped tracksuit with a stripe down each sleeve and leg, mitten hands, white trainers, about desk height. HE WEARS THE REAL KEY, the object photographed on the live set: round head with a three lobed clover hole, three ring collar, shaft, toothed bit. See reference/OBJECT_SHEET_KEY-v2.png. It hangs small, about the size of one of his eyes, and IT IS GOLD AND THE ONLY COLOUR IN THE FILM. The chain stays pencil grey right up to the ring. He wears the thing he later hands over, which is why the key frame lands: he has been carrying it the whole time.

entries.title: The corridor
entries.note: AND ONLY NOW DO WE SEE WHERE HE IS. The camera keeps moving and the building assembles around it: a corridor of doors running away from us, organic architecture in the manner of Gaudi, bone and cartilage rather than brick. The door he came through is already shut behind us and is never shown again. Its name before the reset was 8-0-A-v5. ARCHIVED 4.9.2026. It was 7-2, drawn before the house had a design: hinged wooden doors, organs chosen because a body has organs, and cables on the ceiling. All three are gone.

dna.symbol: THE DOOR, and what a door promises. Six of them in one frame, each swelling with the shape of what waits behind it, so the audience learns to read a bump before anything asks them to. This is the frame that makes the key door work forty seconds later.
dna.composition: ONE POINT PERSPECTIVE, dead centre, and deliberately not the spiral used for the vortex. Every line runs to the bright opening at the end, which is where he is going and what he has not found yet. The book calls symmetry calm and official; here it is used for a house that has been running smoothly for fourteen years without him.
dna.balance: Almost perfectly symmetrical, which is the point. The only asymmetry is the one open door near the vanishing point, and because a small counterweight far out carries real weight, that gap holds the whole frame.

entries.prompt:
The same corridor as the reference, the same warm cream paper and grey pencil, the same vaulted ceiling and rows of pale clay doors receding to a small bright opening at the far end.

One thing is different. Every oval name plaque with writing on it has gone. In place of each, the clay of the door swells outward into a raised shape, moulded in the surface the way a tree is pressed into the wall of an old clay house, catching the light along its upper edge.

Nearest left, a bundle of muscle fibres. Nearest right, a pair of lungs. Beyond them a heart and a coil of gut. No lettering anywhere.

suno.scene: instrumental, no vocals. low sustained drone, one unhurried key, a slow plucked bass note every few bars. patient, warm, nothing hurrying. 60 bpm.
suno.shot: the drone continues and a low frame drum enters, soft, walking pace, one beat per step. no melody yet. no flute. the room is bigger than the music.
suno.why: Root and earth: skin and wood. The walking pulse is the first percussion since the threshold, and it is deliberately not the heartbeat, which is saved for the heart hall.

entries.meaning:
THE FRAME THAT TEACHES THE AUDIENCE TO READ. Nothing is explained here and everything is taught. Six doors carry six shapes and no word appears anywhere, so by the time the audience reaches a door with a key on it they already know what that means and nobody had to tell them.

The written plaques were removed for the reason in WINNING_FILM: a word excludes anybody who does not read English and does not survive translation. A shape raised in clay is read by the body.

It also establishes the house as ordinary and working. This is not a ruin and not a nightmare. The floor is worn down the middle by long use, and the long use is his own.

entries.note: CLOSE ON ONE DOOR. A muscle, pressed into the clay, in the only close look the halls get. entries.prompt:
The same pale clay doorway as the first reference, same paper, same pencil, same soft arch and worn floor and small oval handle.

The plaque and its words are gone completely. In their place the clay swells outward into one large raised shape running the whole height of the door, from just above the floor to the top of the arch: the key from the second reference, seen from the side. Moulded in the same white clay as the door, part of it and not attached to it, no paint, no colour, upper edges catching the light.

suno.why: SPACE, which the book says is what is left when the others stop, and should not be filled. The ordeal is comprehension, so the loudest thing here is the absence of everything else.

entries.meaning:
THE CONFIRMATION, NOT THE SURPRISE. By now the audience can read the doors, so this one does not startle them, it satisfies them. That is a better feeling and a rarer one.

VIVEKA came off the door for this. A name would have told us who; a key tells us what, and what is the thing he came for. He does not know yet that the two are the same.

It is also the last frame of the approach. Everything before it is searching and everything after it is meeting.

entries.title: Viveka, and the first gold
entries.note: He turns to look at us, and on a cord at his neck hangs the key. THE FIRST GOLD IN THE FILM. Gouache over pencil, the only painted thing on the sheet. The film became serious and a small smiling brain could not hold the scene where the argument lands, so Viveka is a person now. The room went with him: three trackballs instead of a hundred switches, a free standing hologram instead of panels on a wall, and one chair instead of two.

entries.note: The vortex drawn as water, long soft strokes sweeping around and inward to an off centre throat, with the keys tiny and scattered and CARRIED by the current rather than building it. entries.prompt:
A hand drawn pencil study on warm cream paper, the same graphite and the same sheet as the reference. Grey graphite only. There is no colour anywhere.

A soft vortex of cloud, seen from below. It rises away from us and turns as it goes, narrowing to a small pale throat high in the upper part of the frame, slightly off centre. It is drawn the way cloud is drawn: long soft strokes made with the side of the pencil, smudged and blended, edges that dissolve rather than end. Light and airy, mostly bare paper, gentle rather than violent.

The frame is otherwise empty. No keys of any kind. No person, no figure, no lettering, no border, no architecture, no floor, no objects of any kind carried in the cloud.
entries.meaning:
THE DOOR OUT OF THE WORLD. The first frame of the second half, and the first thing the audience sees after his eyes close. It does two jobs at once: it convinces them the film has changed, and it explains nothing.

It carries no information on purpose. Nothing to read, no object, no symbol, nothing that could be a clue. Three earlier versions built the vortex out of keys and every one failed for the same reason: a tunnel made of keys tells the audience what he is looking for before he knows it himself, so the film says the word out loud long before he reaches the key door.

Emotionally it is gentle. Not a storm, and he is not in danger. He is being taken, not wrecked, and that softness is what makes the house of the body afterwards read as somewhere he belongs rather than somewhere he has crashed.

It moves the film forward by changing its grammar. Before it, things arrive by frottage. After it, nothing arrives and we travel through surfaces instead. This is the hinge, and it is why there is no cut anywhere after it.

The same vortex returns near the end, going down, when Viveka lets the key go. Rising into it and falling out of it is the shape of the whole second half.

dna.element: WATER, in its cloud form. WINNING_FILM calls water the only element that is both the danger and the cure, and that is exactly the ambiguity this frame needs: it is taking him somewhere he did not ask to go, and it is the only way he gets there. Cloud is water with the weight taken out, which is why it lifts rather than drowns. THRESHOLD is the second element here and it is the one the book says films waste: this is not a door, it is the line under it.
dna.symbol: The turn itself. A spiral says a thing is being drawn toward a centre rather than travelling in a line, and the book notes that the same shape turns up in shells, storms and seed heads, so nobody has to be taught it. It is never explained on screen and never mentioned. Anyone who feels it, feels it.
dna.composition: THE SPIRAL. Chosen because the book says it moves the eye rather than merely placing things, and moving the eye inward is the literal action of the shot. The throat is the tight end and the whole cloud wraps around it, so the audience travels the frame the way Manan travels the vortex. Note the film does not repeat this: the corridors are one point perspective and the credits are symmetrical, because a structure applied identically for two minutes stops being structure and becomes wallpaper.
dna.balance: Deliberately off centre and asymmetrical, which the book pairs with instability. A symmetrical version would read calm and official, which is the wrong feeling for the moment the floor goes out from under the film. Squint at it and the dark mass sits away from the middle, so the picture leans, and the audience feels that without knowing why.
dna.phase: Phase 6 of 15, THE VORTEX UP. The first frame after his eyes close, and the first frame of the second half. Everything before it arrives by frottage; everything after it is travelled through. There is no cut anywhere from here to the end.
dna.journey: CROSSING THE THRESHOLD. Not the door, the line under it. He has spent the first half arguing with the limit and here he stops arguing and goes through, and it is the point of no return: the film never returns him to the bicycle, rested or otherwise. What follows are the tests, three wrong rooms in the house of the body, and the mentor is not met until the very end, inside the cave, because in this film the thing holding him back turns out to be the thing that releases him.

suno.scene: instrumental, no vocals, no percussion. slow ambient raga drone in a single unhurried key, tanpura and a low sustained cello holding one note underneath. gentle, weightless, unresolved. nothing arrives and nothing lands. 60 bpm, feels slower.
suno.shot: the same drone, and above it ONE bansuri flute alone. solo, breathy, unaccompanied, long phrases with audible breath between them, rising and circling rather than going anywhere. no other instrument enters. no percussion at all. the flute is the only thing moving.
suno.why: Air, because this is cloud, and the breath instruments are what air sounds like. The bansuri plays alone because he is alone in it and because a solo has no ground under it, which is the feeling of the floor going out. The drone continues from the scene bed so the music does not restart when the picture changes; only the instrumentation does. Percussion stays out until he arrives in the house, so that the first heartbeat in the film is the heart hall.

entries.note: THE UP VORTEX TURNED 180 DEGREES. A stand in, not a drawing. It is here so the shape of the film can be seen end to end while the real descent is made. Rotating a spiral does reverse the sense of the turn, which is why it holds at all, but the cloud still thins toward what is now the bottom and it will read as upside down once anybody looks twice.

dna.symbol: The same turn, reversed. Nothing new is introduced on the way home.
dna.composition: The spiral again, inverted. This is the ONE place the film is allowed to repeat a composition, because the repetition is the meaning.
dna.balance: Off centre, mirrored from the ascent.

suno.why: He rose to a solo and returns with a pulse under him. The heart he found in the house comes home with him, which is the whole point of a road back.

entries.meaning: THE WAY HOME. He has what he came for and the film has to get him back without inventing a new idea, so it uses the shape it already built. Rising was the loss of ground; falling is the return of it. The key falls beside him rather than in his hand, because the catch has to be his own action and not a delivery.

entries.title: The same frame, inspected
entries.note: THE INSPECTION PRINCIPLE, and it applies to every approved frame from here. Take the frame as it already is, change nothing in it, and lay ONE photorealistic magnifying glass over it with the handle running off the bottom edge so it reads as held from outside the shot. Only what sits BEHIND the lens grows: four or five times up, filling the circle with almost no empty glass, every pencil stroke readable. The lens distorts like real glass, the lines bowing toward the rim with a refracted fringe at the edge, and the magnified image does not line up with the drawing outside it because the glass displaces what is behind it. NEVER a second glass, never a small figure beside a big one, and never a redrawn subject. Each inspection frame sits immediately after the frame it inspects. Sits with 1-4-D-v3 on the scene and breakdown pages rather than on the front page storyboard, because it is built from that frame and a pair split across two pages is not a pair. HELD 3.9.2026: not placed by the running order Baba dictated for scene one, which keeps the leg inspection only. Kept and not cut. One edit puts it back.

entries.title: The avenue, and the finish
entries.note: The wide shot. The avenue runs away between the trees and the banner is small and far off at the vanishing point, which is the whole point of it: he sees the finish from a long way out, while there is still nothing left in him. entries.title: The same finish, through the glass
entries.note: THE GLASS IS ON THE CAMERA LENS, NOT ON THE PAPER. That is the rule this frame establishes and every inspection frame follows it: imagine the magnifying glass held immediately in front of the lens that is shooting the shot. So it is large and close, slightly soft at the rim from being that near, it casts NO shadow on the drawing because it is not touching it, and the world is seen through it and around it. Inside, the distant banner arrives almost at the viewer, F I N filling the circle, bowing outward toward the brass with a refracted fringe at the very edge. entries.title: He goes down

entries.title: The recovery
entries.note: THE INSTANT BETWEEN FALLING AND RUNNING. He has caught his balance and come upright, one foot ahead of the other, arms away from his sides, and his head is up and looking down the road. The face is the whole point: the empty upward stare of the collapse has gone and been replaced by recognition, mouth closed with one corner lifted. He has seen the finish and understood he is going to reach it. He has not started running yet. entries.title: The calf, through the glass
entries.note: INSPECTION FIVE, AND THE LAST ONE IN THE FILM. entries.note: HE ARRIVES THROUGH THE HIP, WHICH IS WHERE A PERSON IS BORN. The hall is the pelvis seen from the front and it reads as two things at once: the iliac blades open on either side like a pair of butterfly wings, with the fanned structure of a wing running through them where the bone grain would be, and the pelvic arch closes underneath. It is waiting, the same way the front door was open, because he is expected. ARCHIVED 4.9.2026: the spine was inside the glass tube, and the lift stopped at the chest.

entries.title: The lift rises, and the body is revealed
entries.note: AND NOW THE REVEAL, THE OPPOSITE WAY ROUND FROM THE ARRIVAL AT THE HOUSE. He steps in, the lift starts, and the camera pulls out until the whole body is in frame and we see how far up he has to go. ONE LIFT AND ONLY ONE, a round glass cylinder running dead straight up the spine from the pelvis to the top of the chest, where the shaft STOPS. He is not searching, he is being carried, which is the same grammar as the vortex: the brain arranged this and nothing about it is effort. No cloud anywhere against the body; it sits only at the foot of the frame with the trace of the vortex under it. ARCHIVED 4.9.2026: the spine was inside the glass tube, and the lift stopped at the chest.

entries.title: He climbs the neck
entries.note: THE ONLY EFFORT IN THE WHOLE JOURNEY. The lift cannot go past the chest, so the neck is climbed: seven cervical vertebrae in grown stone, anatomically correct, with nothing built on them. No steps, no rail, no machinery. The gaps between the transverse processes are the only handholds. Above, the skull closes over and the door is set into the dome, small and lit. He has been carried the whole way and the last stretch he has to do himself, immediately below the door of the man who decides what he is allowed to do. ARCHIVED 4.9.2026: the spine was inside the glass tube, and the lift stopped at the chest.

entries.title: The door, closed
entries.note: THE DOOR, CLOSED. The clover key pressed into the clay above the same sliding panels as every other door in the house, so nothing announces it except what is missing: this is the only door in the building with no status panel beside it, because it is the thing that reads the house rather than a thing the house reads. Centred, and the stone settles differently left and right because it is grown and not built.

entries.title: It opens by itself, and he is in front of it
entries.note: IT OPENS BY ITSELF AND HE DOES NOT TOUCH IT, and he is standing in it. The panels slide apart and what is behind is pure white with no detail in it, so bright that it BLOOMS: the light spills past the opening, washes over the inner edges of the panels and eats the hard edges of the arch away. He is a dark shape against it. THIS IS A COMPOSED SHOT: the boy is keyed in from the live action, so the empty door is kept beside it as the plate. The hall is the pelvis seen from the front and it reads as two things at once: the iliac blades open on either side like a pair of butterfly wings, with the fanned structure of a wing running through them where the bone grain would be, and the pelvic arch closes underneath. entries.note: THE ROOM, AND HE IS IN IT. One chair, and he is sitting in it, on the LEFT of frame looking RIGHT, which is the screen direction this scene never crosses. The console is a colour grading surface rather than a cockpit: three big trackballs in dished rings with fluted wheels, a handful of large keys, and empty surface between them, all sized for a grown man. A wise man does not need hundreds of controls. Above it the display is a HOLOGRAM standing free in the air, no bezel and no housing, a body turning slowly in separated layers with readouts hanging beside it. That is the same body Manan has just ridden up, seen the way Viveka sees it.

The Little Prince grown up: late twenties, slight, not tall, an open face closer to a smile than to a smile, a thick mass of close curls, and the star cloak worn open over plain clothes. Reference, not a shot.

entries.title: Manan's theory, visualised
entries.note: HE NEVER WRITES IT DOWN. He thinks it and VIVEKA VISUALISES IT, because Viveka can read him, which is why there is no board in this room and never was. The hologram shows the old theory as somebody else's idea being displayed rather than Viveka's own: the standing body with ONE LEG MUSCLE LIT and everything else dim, the gauge hard over at empty, the line falling away to nothing. Fatigue is in the muscle, the fuel is spent, the tank reads empty. NO WRITING ANYWHERE: the argument is made in pictures because the dialogue carries every word already.

entries.note: AND HIS ANSWER IN THE SAME PLACES, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE PAIR. The identical arrangement with every value reversed: the head lit and the leg dim, the same gauge in the same corner with the needle still well up, the same line levelling off deliberately part way down instead of collapsing. Fatigue is in the brain, and when he stops you the fuel is still there. Nothing about the layout may move between the two frames; the rhyme is the argument.

dialogue.speaker: VIVEKA

flight_note: FROM PHASE 5 ONWARD THE FILM DOES NOT CUT, IT FLIES. Think of an aeroplane going through cloud: you do not arrive by cutting, you arrive by passing through something. We fly in toward his head as his eyes close, pass into white, rise through the vortex, arrive at the door, and he is drawn through it rather than walking in. Then we fly backwards and the house assembles around what we have just entered, fly on through the rooms, and land at the skull door. The landing is the only stop, because the conversation needs stillness. Then we fly at the banner and through it, and the key is given in the white on the other side. The credits fly too, card to card, through cloud. IF A BEAT SEEMS TO NEED A CUT, LOOK AGAIN: there is nearly always a surface to pass through, and there is no exception anywhere. The key falls the whole way and the camera never leaves it. Viveka's hand and Manan's never share a frame because an entire descent lies between them, which is better than a cut: a cut is a decision the audience can feel, a fall is one they take with the object. THE MEMORIES BEHIND THE FALL ARE MOTION BLURRED, streaked vertically in the direction of the fall, because they are passing at speed. Not so much that they become mush: you must still be able to make out what each one is if you look for it. THE KEY STAYS SHARP, because the camera is travelling with it, and that difference between the sharp key and the streaked world is what makes the fall read as fast.
rubbing_note: THE FIRST HALF DOES NOT GET DRAWN ON SCREEN, IT SURFACES. Think of a coin under a sheet of paper and a pencil rubbed across it until the shape comes through. Parts arrive one at a time and in an order that is a law, not a preference: WHAT SUPPORTS COMES FIRST. NATURE IS BUILT BEFORE ANYBODY STANDS IN IT. The road first, because without the road there are no trees beside it. Then the trees. Then the shoes standing on the road, then the legs, and last of all the man. A shoe cannot appear before the road it stands on. Ground before figure, and the thing he stands on before the thing that stands. Each part comes up out of blank paper in a few frames and then simply is. USE IT ONLY TO OPEN A SCENE. It is how the drawn world comes into existence, so it happens once at the start and then stops; from the next frame on, the animation is ordinary. It returns exactly once more, on the first frame of the muscle sequence, because that is a second world being entered. Anywhere else it becomes decoration and stops meaning anything. It is cheap to make, which is the point: a few frames of an image resolving is a filter and a mask, not drawn inbetweens. SO THE FILM HAS ONE GRAMMAR PER HALF. Before he closes his eyes, things arrive: the world is manifested out of paper. After he closes his eyes, nothing arrives and we move instead: every transition is a passage through a surface. One is the world coming to him, the other is him going through the world.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: A boy runs. Not a race, not a competition, just a boy on a road. And the world he runs through does not appear the way drawings usually appear. It surfaces. Like a coin under paper with a pencil rubbed over it, things come up out of the blank sheet one at a time, and always in the same order: the road first, then the shoes standing on it, then the legs, then the trees, and the man last of all. What holds a thing up must exist before the thing. This happens once, to open the film, and then it stops.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: He rides a bicycle. He tests where his limit is, again and again. He gets tired, and he meets the wall.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: He closes his eyes.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: From that moment the film changes its rules and never changes them back. Before, things came to him. Now nothing arrives and we move instead. Every change of place is a passage through a surface, and there is not one cut left in the film. We fly into his head as his eyes shut, through white, and a vortex takes him upward, out of the world.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: He arrives at a door already giving off light, and he is drawn through it rather than walking in. We pull back and the house assembles around us, and by the time we can see the whole building the door is shut. It is a house made of his own body.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: We fly along its corridors. The doors do not have names on them. They have shapes pressed into the clay: a muscle, a pair of lungs, a heart. He looks in each room, and there is nothing in it for him.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Then a door with a key on it. And he goes in.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Inside, a small brain in a chair at a wall of dials. And he has been waiting.

radio_drama.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama.text: Ah. There you are. I was expecting you.

radio_drama.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama.text: Before we start. Lift your right arm for me.

radio_drama.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama.text: I'm trying.

radio_drama.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama.text: I know.

radio_drama.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama.text: I can't. Why can't I move it?

radio_drama.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama.text: Try now.

radio_drama.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama.text: That was you. It was never my arm at all.

radio_drama.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama.text: It is always your arm. The permission is mine.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Then the two of them put it on the boards. Neither board arrives finished. Manan writes what he was taught, in white chalk, line by line: the old theory. Viveka answers on the whiteboard in black marker. The same layout, the same three lines, the same gauge, and every single value reversed.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: They reach a conclusion together. Then the vortex takes him back down, and the key falls with him.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Viveka lets it go, and it falls through an empty frame. It turns and it grows as it comes, and behind it the whole film replays in reverse, so faint it is almost not there: the boards, the room, the house, and the avenue as it lands. The memories are streaked in the direction of the fall because they are passing at speed, but you can still make out what each one is if you look. The key stays sharp, because the camera is falling with it, and that difference is what makes the fall feel fast.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: On the way down it crosses from a pencil drawing to a photograph, and no single frame is the moment it becomes real.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Manan catches it at the bottom.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama.text: Their two hands are never in the same frame, because an entire descent lies between them. That is deliberate, and it is better than a cut. A cut is a decision the audience can feel. A fall is one they take with the object.

radio_drama.speaker: NARRATOR

radio_drama_hr.text: Dječak trči. Nije utrka, nije natjecanje, samo dječak na cesti. A svijet kroz koji trči ne pojavljuje se onako kako se crteži obično pojavljuju. On izranja. Kao novčić ispod papira preko kojeg se olovkom trlja, stvari izlaze iz praznog lista jedna po jedna, i uvijek istim redom. Prvo cesta, pa cipele koje na njoj stoje, pa noge, pa drveće, i tek na kraju čovjek. Ono što nešto drži mora postojati prije te stvari. To se dogodi jednom, da otvori film, i onda prestane.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Vozi bicikl. Ispituje gdje mu je granica, opet i opet. Umara se, i nailazi na zid.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Zatvara oči.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Od tog trenutka film mijenja svoja pravila i više ih ne vraća. Prije su stvari dolazile k njemu. Sada ništa ne dolazi, nego se mi krećemo. Svaka promjena mjesta je prolazak kroz površinu, i u filmu više nema nijednog reza. Ulijećemo mu u glavu dok se oči zatvaraju, kroz bijelo, i vrtlog ga podiže prema gore, izvan svijeta.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Stiže pred vrata koja već svijetle, i biva uvučen kroz njih umjesto da ušeta. Odmičemo se, i kuća se sklapa oko nas, a dok vidimo cijelu zgradu vrata su već zatvorena. To je kuća sagrađena od njegova vlastitog tijela.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Letimo njezinim hodnicima. Vrata nemaju imena na sebi. Imaju oblike utisnute u glinu: mišić, pluća, srce. Zaviruje u svaku sobu, i ni u jednoj nema ničega za njega.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Onda vrata s ključem na sebi. I ulazi.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Unutra, mali mozak u stolici pred zidom punim brojčanika. I on ga je čekao.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_hr.text: Ah. Tu si. Očekivao sam te.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_hr.text: Prije nego počnemo. Podigni mi desnu ruku.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Pokušavam.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_hr.text: Znam.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Ne mogu. Zašto je ne mogu pomaknuti?

radio_drama_hr.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_hr.text: Probaj sada.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: To si bio ti. Nikada to nije ni bila moja ruka.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_hr.text: Ruka je uvijek tvoja. Dopuštenje je moje.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Onda njih dvojica to iznose na ploče. Nijedna ploča ne dolazi gotova. Manan bijelom kredom piše ono što su ga učili, redak po redak. Stara teorija.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Tisuću devetsto dvadeset treća. Hill stavlja trkače na traku i mjeri sve što rade. Njegov odgovor je jednostavan. Umor je u mišiću.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Trčiš. Mišić troši svoj kisik. Gorivo se potroši. I kad spremnik pokaže prazno, tijelo stane.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Viveka odgovara na bijeloj ploči crnim markerom. Isti raspored, ista tri retka, isti mjerač, i svaka vrijednost obrnuta.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_hr.text: Puls, dah, temperatura, voda, udaljenost. Čitam sve to, cijelo vrijeme. I postavljam jedno pitanje: možemo li nastaviti sigurno?

radio_drama_hr.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_hr.text: Kad odgovor počne izgledati kao ne, usporim te. Dakle ne. Umor je u mozgu, a ne u tvojim nogama. Ovdje gore. I odlučuje mnogo prije nego što je išta stvarno u opasnosti.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_hr.text: Kad te ja zaustavim, gorivo je još uvijek tu.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Znači zid...

radio_drama_hr.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_hr.text: Je broj koji sam ja odabrao. Pažljivo. Da te održim na životu.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_hr.text: Onda to može biti i drugi broj.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Dolaze do zaključka zajedno. Onda ga vrtlog nosi natrag dolje, i ključ pada s njim.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Viveka ga pušta, i on pada kroz prazan kadar. Okreće se i raste dok dolazi, a iza njega se cijeli film vrti unatrag, tako blijedo da ga gotovo nema. Ploče, soba, kuća, i drvored dok slijeće. Sjećanja su razvučena u smjeru pada jer prolaze brzinom, ali još uvijek možeš razabrati što je svako od njih ako pogledaš. Ključ ostaje oštar, jer kamera pada s njim, i ta razlika je ono što čini da pad djeluje brzo.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Na putu prema dolje prelazi iz crteža olovkom u fotografiju, i nijedan pojedini kadar nije trenutak u kojem postaje stvaran.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Manan ga hvata na dnu.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Njihove dvije ruke nikada nisu u istom kadru, jer između njih leži cijeli pad. To je namjerno, i bolje je od reza. Rez je odluka koju publika osjeti. Pad je odluka koju uzmu zajedno s predmetom.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Odjavna špica, od kartice do kartice, kroz oblake.

radio_drama_hr.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_hr.text: Posvećeno Gospodinu Ganeshi. Uklonitelju prepreka.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Maratonac trči. Duga cesta, ravnomjeran korak, čovjek koji ovo radi cijeli život.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: I onda ga gledamo kako se raspada.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Korak mu se lomi. Ramena padaju. Glava mu visi. Noge više ne slušaju kako treba, i svaki sljedeći korak izgleda kao da bi mogao biti zadnji. Posrće. Pada. Diže se, i trči dalje, ali to više nije trčanje, to je čovjek koji se odbija zaustaviti.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Prazan je. Nema više ništa u njemu. Svatko tko ovo gleda zna kako to izgleda kad je gotovo.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: A onda, na kraju ceste, nešto se pojavi.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: I on ga vidi.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Traka. Natpis preko ceste. Cilj.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: I čovjek koji prije pet sekundi nije imao ništa, sada sprinta. Glava gore, ramena natrag, korak kratak i brz. Sprinta prema traci brže nego što je trčao cijelu utrku.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Trči, i istrči van kadra.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Ostane prazan papir.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Onda se na taj prazan papir vrati prizor od maloprije. Čovjek dolje na cesti, zaustavljen, kao fotografija koju je netko stavio pred nas da je pogledamo.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: A u taj zaleđeni kadar ušeta dječak.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Manan. S povećalom u ruci, kao netko tko je upravo ušao na mjesto zločina. Okrene se prema nama, da vidimo što će raditi.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Pa stavi povećalo na lice. Prvo na ono prazno lice s početka. Oko poluzatvoreno pod teškom obrvom, usta otvorena, crte urezane duboko.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Pa na lice iz trenutka kad je nešto vidio. Glava gore, oko širom otvoreno, obrve skupljene.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Pa na lice poslije toga. Oko mirno, crte omekšale, osmijeh u kutu usana.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Tri lica istog čovjeka, u razmaku od nekoliko sekundi. Nitko mu ništa nije dao između njih.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: A onda se dogodi ono što je srce ovog filma. Trenutak u kojem se nešto otpusti.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Kamera ulazi u njega. Koža postaje prozirna, kao da je papir kroz koji se vidi, i pod njom se ukaže cijela građa: mišići, vlakna, tetive, sve isprepleteno i sve umorno. Mrtvo. Sivo.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: I onda se upali.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Prvo jedan mišić u listu, kao žica koja je dobila struju. Pa drugi, iznad njega. Pa cijelo bedro. Svjetlo putuje kroz njegovo tijelo, od stopala prema gore, mišić po mišić, kao da negdje netko jedan po jedan pušta prekidače. Ono što je sekundu prije bilo sivo, sada gori.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Nije to novo gorivo. Nije mu nitko ništa dao. To je bilo tu cijelo vrijeme, samo zatvoreno, i netko je upravo odlučio otvoriti.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Koža se vraća. Svjetlo ostaje ispod nje.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: I čovjek otrči van kadra. Ostane prazan papir, kao i prvi put.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Odakle mu to? Spremnik je bio prazan. Vidjeli smo da je bio prazan.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Ako je gorivo bilo potrošeno, odakle sprint? A ako sprint postoji, onda gorivo nije bilo potrošeno. Netko je lagao.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Ovdje film dobiva svoju temu. Nije riječ o čovjeku koji trči, nego o dječaku koji želi znati zašto čovjek stane, i zašto odjednom prestane stajati.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Radoznalost postaje pokus. Izvodi bicikl na ulicu i sam gura granicu, jer pitanje na kojem možeš voziti bolje je od pitanja koje možeš samo čitati.

radio_drama_v7.text: Onda u sobi, na trenažeru, s vlastitom ranijom vožnjom koja se vrti na laptopu pred njim. Utrkuje se sam sa sobom. Nema protivnika, nema sata, nitko ne gleda. radio_drama_v7.text: Tisuću devetsto dvadeset treća. Hill stavlja trkače na traku i mjeri sve što rade. Njegov odgovor je jednostavan. Umor je u mišiću.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v7.text: Trčiš. Mišić troši svoj kisik. Gorivo se potroši. I kad spremnik pokaže prazno, tijelo stane.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Viveka odgovara na bijeloj ploči crnim markerom. Isti raspored, ista tri retka, isti mjerač, i svaka vrijednost obrnuta.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_v7.text: Puls, dah, temperatura, voda, udaljenost. Čitam sve to, cijelo vrijeme. I postavljam jedno pitanje: možemo li nastaviti sigurno?

radio_drama_v7.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_v7.text: Kad odgovor počne izgledati kao ne, usporim te. Dakle ne. Umor je u mozgu, a ne u tvojim nogama. Ovdje gore. I odlučuje mnogo prije nego što je išta stvarno u opasnosti.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_v7.text: Kad te ja zaustavim, gorivo je još uvijek tu.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Manan kaže.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v7.text: Znači zid...

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Viveka kaže.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_v7.text: Je broj koji sam ja odabrao. Pažljivo. Da te održim na životu.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Manan kaže.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_v7.text: Onda to može biti i drugi broj.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Dolaze do zaključka zajedno. Onda ga vrtlog nosi natrag dolje, i ključ pada s njim.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Viveka ga pušta, i on pada kroz prazan kadar. Okreće se i raste dok dolazi, a iza njega se cijeli film vrti unatrag, tako blijedo da ga gotovo nema. Ploče, soba, kuća, i drvored dok slijeće. Sjećanja su razvučena u smjeru pada jer prolaze brzinom, ali još uvijek možeš razabrati što je svako od njih ako pogledaš. Ključ ostaje oštar, jer kamera pada s njim, i ta razlika je ono što čini da pad djeluje brzo.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Na putu prema dolje prelazi iz crteža olovkom u fotografiju, i nijedan pojedini kadar nije trenutak u kojem postaje stvaran.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Manan ga hvata na dnu.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Odjavna špica, od kartice do kartice, kroz oblake.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: I ako se sada odmakneš i pogledaš cijeli film odjednom, vidiš da je to putovanje. Prvo trči. Onda vozi. Onda leti. Uspinje se, sve više i više. A onda pada.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: To je stari oblik, stariji od filma. Junak se uzdiže, junak umire, i junak se vraća s nečim što prije nije imao. Manan se vraća s ključem. I sa spoznajom da zid nije zid, nego postavka. Broj koji je netko odabrao, i koji se može promijeniti.

radio_drama_v7.speaker: NARATOR
radio_drama_v7.text: Posvećeno Gospodinu Ganeshi. Uklonitelju prepreka.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: A marathon runner. A long road, an even stride, a man who has done this all his life.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: And then we watch him come apart.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: His stride breaks. The shoulders drop. The head hangs. The legs stop doing what they are told, and every next step looks like it could be the last one. He stumbles. He goes down.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: He is empty. There is nothing left in him, and anyone watching this knows what it looks like when it is over.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: And then, at the end of the road, something appears.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: And he sees it.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: A banner. Stretched across the road. The finish.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: And the man who five seconds ago had nothing is sprinting. Head up, shoulders back, the stride short and fast. Sprinting for that banner faster than he ran the whole race.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: He runs, and he runs out of the frame.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: What is left is empty paper.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Then onto that empty paper comes the thing we saw a moment ago. The man down on the road, stopped, like a photograph somebody has put in front of us to look at.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: And into that stopped picture, a boy walks in.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Manan. A magnifying glass in his hand, like somebody who has just arrived at a crime scene. He turns to us, so we can see what he is going to do.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Then he puts the glass on the face. First on the empty face from the beginning. The eye half shut under a heavy brow, the mouth open, the lines cut deep.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Then on the face from the moment he saw something. The head up, the eye wide open, the brows drawn together.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Then on the face after that. The eye calm, the lines softened, a smile at the corner of the mouth.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Three faces of the same man, seconds apart. Nobody gave him anything in between.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: And then the thing happens that is the heart of this film. The moment something lets go.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: The camera goes into him. The skin turns transparent, like paper you can see through, and underneath it the whole structure shows: muscle, fibre, tendon, all of it woven together and all of it tired. Dead. Grey.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: And then it lights up.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: One muscle in the calf first, like a wire that has been given current. Then another above it. Then the whole thigh. Light travels up through his body, muscle by muscle, as though somewhere somebody is throwing switches one at a time. What was grey a second ago is burning.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: It is not new fuel. Nobody gave him anything. It was there the whole time, only closed, and somebody has just decided to open it.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: The skin comes back. The light stays underneath it.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: And the man runs out of the frame. What is left is empty paper, the same as the first time.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Where did that come from? The tank was empty. We saw that it was empty.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: If the fuel was spent, where did the sprint come from? And if the sprint exists, then the fuel was not spent. Somebody lied.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: This is where the film finds its subject. It is not about a man who runs. It is about a boy who wants to know why a man stops, and why he suddenly stops stopping.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Curiosity turns into an experiment. He takes the bicycle out into the street and pushes the limit himself, because a question you can ride is better than a question you can only read.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Then indoors, on the trainer, with his own earlier ride playing on the laptop in front of him. He is racing himself. No opponent, no clock, nobody watching. The only thing he is trying to beat is what his own body did an hour ago. He pushes until he collapses.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: He closes his eyes.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: From that moment the film changes its rules and never changes them back. Before, things came to him. Now nothing arrives and we move instead. Every change of place is a passage through a surface, and there is not one cut left in the film. We fly into his head as the eyes close, through white, and a vortex lifts him up, out of the world.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: He arrives at a door that is already giving off light, and he is pulled through it rather than walking in. We draw back, and the house assembles around us, and by the time we can see the whole building the door is already shut. It is a house built out of his own body.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: We fly along its corridors. The doors have no names on them. They have shapes pressed into the clay: a muscle, a pair of lungs, a heart. He looks into every room, and in none of them is there anything for him.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Then a door with a key on it. And he goes in.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Inside, a small brain in a chair in front of a wall of dials. And he has been expecting him.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Viveka says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_en.text: Ah. There you are. I was expecting you.

radio_drama_en.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_en.text: Before we begin. Raise my right arm.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Manan says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_en.text: I am trying.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Viveka says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_en.text: I know.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Manan says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_en.text: I can't. Why can't I move it?

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Viveka says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_en.text: Try now.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Manan says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_en.text: That was you. It was never my arm at all.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Viveka says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_en.text: The arm is always yours. The permission is mine.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Then the two of them take it to the boards. Neither board arrives finished. Manan writes what he was taught in white chalk, line by line. The old theory.

radio_drama_en.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_en.text: Nineteen twenty three. Hill puts runners on a treadmill and measures everything they do. His answer is simple. Fatigue is in the muscle.

radio_drama_en.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_en.text: You run. The muscle uses up its oxygen. The fuel is spent. And when the tank reads empty, the body stops.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Viveka answers on the white board in black marker. The same layout, the same three lines, the same gauge, and every value reversed.

radio_drama_en.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_en.text: Pulse, breath, temperature, water, distance. I read all of it, the whole time. And I ask one question: can we carry on safely?

radio_drama_en.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_en.text: When the answer starts to look like no, I slow you down. So, no. Fatigue is in the brain, not in your legs. Up here. And it decides long before anything is actually in danger.

radio_drama_en.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_en.text: When I stop you, the fuel is still there.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Manan says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_en.text: So the wall...

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Viveka says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: VIVEKA
radio_drama_en.text: Is a number I chose. Carefully. To keep you alive.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Manan says.

radio_drama_en.speaker: MANAN
radio_drama_en.text: Then it can be a different number.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: They come to the conclusion together. Then the vortex carries him back down, and the key falls with him.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Viveka lets it go, and it falls through an empty frame. It turns and grows as it comes, and behind it the whole film runs backwards, so faint it is almost not there. The boards, the room, the house, and the avenue of trees as it lands. The memories are stretched in the direction of the fall because they are passing at speed, but you can still make out what each one is if you look. The key stays sharp, because the camera is falling with it, and that difference is what makes the fall feel fast.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: On the way down it crosses from a pencil drawing into a photograph, and no single frame is the moment it becomes real.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Manan catches it at the bottom.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: End credits, card to card, through cloud.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: And if you step back now and look at the whole film at once, you see that it is a journey. First he runs. Then he rides. Then he flies. He climbs, higher and higher. And then he falls.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: That is an old shape, older than film. The hero rises, the hero dies, and the hero comes back with something he did not have before. Manan comes back with a key. And with knowing that the wall is not a wall. It is a setting. A number somebody chose, and it can be changed.

radio_drama_en.speaker: NARRATOR
radio_drama_en.text: Dedicated to Lord Ganesha. Remover of obstacles.

flow_guide.label: The title
flow_guide.text: The title, one frame, drawn in the film's own hand on cream paper. Nothing moves. Hold it long enough to read once and cut. If you animate anything here let it be the last pencil stroke settling, and even that is optional. A book being opened, not a film starting.

flow_guide.label: The run, and the collapse
flow_guide.text: Scene one opens wide on an avenue with a man already down at the far end. Cut close to his legs sliding out from under him, then the whole figure. Three faces: spent, then something seen, then a smile. The finish banner. Then he runs, and he runs clean out of frame and leaves the page empty. Animate the collapse HEAVY. It has weight, and everything after the ignition has none. The empty page at one ten is a beat, not a gap, so hold it.

flow_guide.label: Manan arrives, and inspects
flow_guide.text: Now the collapse comes back onto that empty page and Manan walks into it. This is the first time the picture admits it is a picture, and THE ONLY THING THAT MOVES IN THESE FRAMES IS THE BOY. Everything drawn stays absolutely still, and the stiller you keep it the better he reads. Play him curious rather than clever: he has not solved anything, he has only noticed that something does not add up. He inspects the same three faces through the glass, and then the leg fires and the light travels UP through the body muscle by muscle, in order, not all at once. Skin returns, the light stays under it, and he runs out of frame and leaves the page empty a second time.

flow_guide.label: He takes the question outside
flow_guide.text: He cannot let it go, so he takes the question outside and puts it on himself. This phase is the hero plates for the road and the bicycle: what the world looks like before anybody rides through it. Keep it ordinary. This is the last daylight in the film and everything after it is inside his head.

flow_guide.label: The bicycle, and the trainer
flow_guide.text: The bicycle, shot for real. He is testing the limit on himself, because a question you can ride beats a question you can only read. Keep it young and slightly reckless rather than athletic and let the cut rhythm quicken with him. Then indoors on the trainer, racing his own earlier ride on the laptop. Cut tighter and closer than the street: the room should shrink around him. When the wall arrives, let it arrive SUDDENLY, do not fade into it.

flow_guide.label: He lets go
flow_guide.text: He stops, breathes, and lets go. Out to white. This is the hinge of the whole film and it should feel like relief, not defeat. Slow everything down, take the sound away BEFORE the picture goes, and let the white come up from behind him rather than washing over him. This is the last cut for a long time: nothing cuts again until he comes back down.

flow_guide.label: The vortex, up
flow_guide.text: The vortex, going up. He is carried, not falling, and one detail carries that entirely: his sweatshirt and his hair stream DOWNWARD past him, because the air is going the other way. Lose that and the shot reads as a fall. He is full colour and the world is graphite; colour is under half a per cent of the frame and all of it is him. The vortex opens, he passes, and it closes exactly as it opened.

flow_guide.label: Viveka's room
flow_guide.text: The lift opens and he is in the head. One room, one chair, and a man in it who has been expecting him. THIS IS NOT THE LITTLE BRAIN ANY MORE. Viveka is the Little Prince grown up: late twenties, slight, not tall, an open face closer to a smile than to a smile, and a thick mass of close curls that will remind you of the convolutions of a brain if you let it, though it is only hair. His cloak carries the night sky, small stars and faint constellations and a few ringed planets worked into the weave, because the pineal gland is the portal to the cosmos and the cloak is where the film says so. Play him KIND and play him the most powerful thing in the building, and do not let either cancel the other. Nothing stern, nothing grand, and nothing like a wizard. The room says the same thing the man does. A wise man does not need hundreds of controls, so the console is three big trackballs in dished rings, a handful of large keys, and empty surface between them, all sized for a grown man's hands. Above it the display is a HOLOGRAM standing free in the air with no frame and no housing: a body turning slowly in separated layers, skeleton, muscle, organs, skin, with thin readouts hanging beside it. That is the same body Manan has just ridden up, seen the way Viveka sees it. ONE CHAIR. There used to be two and it was an error nobody questioned for weeks. Screen direction is fixed and never crosses: Viveka on the LEFT looking RIGHT, Manan on the RIGHT looking LEFT. Ah. There you are. I was expecting you. Direction. Then he asks for something impossible, and the whole idea of the film gets done as a party trick instead of a lecture. The boy's arm must genuinely not move. Animate the EFFORT, not the failure. Before we begin. Raise my right arm. I am trying. I know. I can't. Why can't I move it? Try now. That was you. It was never my arm at all. The arm is always yours. The permission is mine.

flow_guide.label: The two theories
flow_guide.text: There is no board in this room and there never was. MANAN NEVER WRITES ANYTHING DOWN. He thinks it, and Viveka visualises it on the hologram that has been standing over the console since he walked in, because Viveka can read him. Then Viveka answers by visualising his own. That is why the chalk and the marker are gone: two boards in a room with a holographic display was one idea too many, and the display was already there. You run. The muscle uses up its oxygen. The fuel is spent. And when the tank reads empty, the body stops. Direction. His idea comes up in the air as somebody else's: the body turning, ONE LEG MUSCLE LIT and everything else dim, the gauge hard over at empty, the line falling away to nothing. Then Viveka answers, and here is the rule that matters more than anything else in the scene. THE SECOND DISPLAY IS THE FIRST ONE WITH EVERY VALUE REVERSED. Same layout, same three elements in the same places, the same gauge in the same corner. The head lit and the leg dim. The needle still well up. The same line, but levelling off deliberately instead of collapsing. Do not move anything between the two, because the rhyme IS the argument. Pulse, breath, temperature, water, sugar. I read all of it, the whole time. That is what every one of those panels you walked past is for. And I ask one question with it. Can we carry on safely? When the answer starts to look like no, I slow you down. Not because anything has run out. Because of where it is heading. Heading. I do not wait for the tank to empty. I watch how fast it is emptying, and I stop you while there is still enough left to get you home. So no. Fatigue is in the brain, not in your legs. Up here. And it decides long before anything is actually in danger. When I stop you, the fuel is still there. Direction. And now the climb pays off. He answers from the rooms he passed on the way up, so hold him wide enough that we remember he has been somewhere. It was. I saw it. The sugar cellar was full. The fat store was barely touched. The fibres were not torn. No. They never are. So the wall... Is a number I chose. Carefully. To keep you alive. Then it can be a different number. Neither display carries a single word, on purpose. The boards had to be READ, which meant translating them. The holograms argue in pictures, a body, a lit part, a gauge and a line, and the dialogue carries every word already. Nothing is lost and it needs no second version.

flow_guide.label: The conclusion
flow_guide.text: The conclusion and the goodbye. Keep it a conversation and not a banner. Nobody wins. The boy is not given the answer, he arrives at it himself and Viveka lets him. Quiet, warm, and short. This section is still one frame and it is waiting on a decision, so do not build on it yet.

flow_guide.label: The fall
flow_guide.text: The vortex down, and the key falls with him. He is falling now, not carried, so the trail REVERSES: everything streams upward past him. The key turns and grows as it comes, and behind it the whole film runs backwards, so faint it is almost not there. Keep the key sharp while everything behind it smears, because the camera is falling with the key and not with the memories. That difference is the entire reason the fall reads as fast.

flow_guide.label: He catches it
flow_guide.text: He catches it. On the way down the key crosses from a pencil drawing into a photograph, and NO SINGLE FRAME is the moment it becomes real; spread it across the fall. Viveka's hand and Manan's are never on screen together, on purpose, so nothing has to be composited and no lighting has to match. The key is the only gold in the film. Everything it lands in should be still.

flow_guide.label: Into the body, and up
flow_guide.text: The house is vertical now, because a body is not a hallway with rooms off it. He arrives through the hip, which is where a person is born: the hall is the pelvis seen from the front, the iliac blades opening either side like a pair of butterfly wings, and the round glass lift standing dead on the axis in the opening a body actually comes through. It is already waiting for him, the same way the front door was already open. He steps in, the lift starts, and now the camera PULLS OUT, the opposite way round from the arrival, until the whole body is in frame and we see how far up he has to go. One lift and only one, straight up the spine, and he is not searching. He is being carried, which is the same grammar as the vortex. The brain arranged this and none of it is effort.

flow_guide.label: The climb, and the door
flow_guide.text: The lift cannot go past the chest, so the neck is climbed. Seven cervical vertebrae, anatomically correct, nothing built on them, and the gaps between the transverse processes are the only handholds. This is the only effort in the whole journey and it lands immediately below the door of the man who decides what he is allowed to do. Then three frames on that door and TWO OF THEM ARE THE SAME PICTURE. Closed. Open, by itself, with the light behind it so bright it blooms past the edges and eats the arch away, and he does not touch it. Then closed again, exactly the frame it opened from. Hold each of the three; the repeat is the point and a variation would spoil it.
